summary: Ppp2r1a perturbation in L5-6 IT glutamatergic cells had a small mixed response with 13 downstream DEGs, led by Hspb3 and Hdac4 up-regulation and Leng8, Son, Cadm1, and Kif21a down-regulation. Searches for a Ppp2r1a link to this heat-shock/HDAC4/RNA-processing and adhesion pattern did not find a direct or partial target-to-response bridge.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic cells produced 715 downstream DEGs with Amy1, Asph, Car4, Daglb, Cyp46a1, and Jun increased and Sorl1 reduced. Ppp2r1a haploinsufficiency alters excitatory synapses, PP2A loss can activate ERK/JNK-c-Jun, and PPP2R1A blockade can feed into SREBP1 lipid signaling, but those papers do not decisively predict the mixed Amy1/RNA-processing/cholesterol direction in this acute neuronal screen.

Ppp2r1a loss in L2-3 IT CTX glutamatergic cells yielded 394 downstream DEGs including Nptx2, Elmo1, Amy1, Daglb, Bdnf, and Jun up-regulation with Itm2c down-regulation. Forebrain Ppp2r1a haploinsufficiency perturbs excitatory synaptic/endocannabinoid biology and PP2A inhibition can activate c-Jun, but neither source connects Ppp2r1a loss to these Bdnf/Nptx2/Itm2c transcript changes with a defined direction.

cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
summary: Ppp2r1a perturbation in L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic cells changed 18 downstream genes, most notably increasing Insig1, Sqle, Dhcr24, and Amy1 while decreasing Fam131a. PPP2R1A loss of function can derepress SREBP1-dependent lipogenesis in liver cancer models, but the connection to neuronal cholesterol regulators rather than hepatic fatty-acid synthesis is incomplete.

cell_type: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
summary: Ppp2r1a perturbation in L2-3 IT PIR/AON/ENT glutamatergic cells gave only 9 downstream DEGs, centered on Amy1, Ccl25, Arhgap29, and Polr3k increases with Las1l and Gpatch8 decreases. Searches for Ppp2r1a connections to Amy1, Ccl25, Arhgap29, Las1l, or Polr3k did not identify a biologically specific bridge.

The only downstream DEG after Ppp2r1a perturbation in MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic cells was Stmn4 up-regulation. A pair-level search for Ppp2r1a regulation of Stmn4 or stathmin-family mRNA did not find a direct or indirect target-to-response relationship.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic cells had a single downstream significant gene, Glrx2, which was decreased. Searches for Ppp2r1a or PP2A Aalpha regulation of Glrx2 did not find a specific literature bridge.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in L5 ET CTX glutamatergic cells produced 68 downstream DEGs dominated by decreases in Sorl1, Dclk1, Tubb3, Snap25, and Stxbp2. A mouse forebrain-excitatory Ppp2r1a haploinsufficiency model documents altered synaptic physiology, but it does not show that acute Ppp2r1a loss should repress this Sorl1/tubulin/synaptic transcript module.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic cells changed 11 genes including Rnpc3, Amy1, Msmo1, and Cyp46a1 increases with Gpatch8 and Snap25 decreases. Ppp2r1a loss is linked to excitatory synaptic dysfunction and PPP2R1A disruption can feed SREBP1 lipid programs, but the specific Rnpc3/Amy1/cholesterol response and its direction remain indirect.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CTX-CGE GABA cells had 10 downstream DEGs, with Stmn4, Amy1, Col26a1, Jun, and Rnpc3 increased and Nmt2 decreased. Neuronal PP2A inhibition activates ERK/JNK signaling and nuclear c-Jun, but that catalytic-subunit model does not establish that loss of the PPP2R1A scaffold drives this mixed Stmn4/Amy1/Rnpc3 signature.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in Pvalb GABA cells produced 30 downstream DEGs, led by Stmn4, Scg2, and Jun up-regulation with Pabpn1 and Kifc2 down-regulation. PP2A inhibition is known to activate ERK/JNK-c-Jun in neurons, but the literature does not connect the Ppp2r1a scaffold to the dominant Stmn4/RNA-processing response.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in Sst GABA cells yielded three downstream increases: Stmn4, Jun, and Pitpnm2. Published neuronal PP2A inhibition predicts increased c-Jun signaling, but transfer from catalytic PP2A inhibition to acute Ppp2r1a loss is incomplete and Stmn4/Pitpnm2 mRNA induction is not documented.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CNU-MGE GABA cells produced 27 downstream DEGs, with Ovgp1 increased and Rsrp1, Snap25, Kifc2, Cbarp, and Tubb2a decreased. Pair-specific searches did not find Ppp2r1a or PPP2R1A evidence for this Ovgp1/Rsrp1/Kifc2/tubulin response.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells had three downstream increases: Igsf9b, Stmn4, and Scn1b. Searches for Ppp2r1a links to Igsf9b, Stmn4, or Scn1b did not identify a target-specific or partial mechanistic bridge.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY GABA cells changed 52 downstream genes including decreases in Leng8, Pabpn1, and Kifc2 and increases in Pcsk1n, Col4a1, and Jun. PP2A inhibition can increase neuronal c-Jun signaling, but the dominant RNA-processing and extracellular-matrix shifts are not a direct documented consequence of Ppp2r1a loss.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic cells produced 137 downstream DEGs, with Pabpn1, Leng8, Ache, and Tubb2a down and Pcsk1n, Insig1, and Jun up. The Jun and Insig1 components have partial support from PP2A-JNK and PPP2R1A-SREBP1 studies, but neither bridge explains the main RNA-processing/tubulin module or gives a decisive neuronal direction.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in MH-LH/TH glutamatergic cells changed 42 downstream genes dominated by down-regulated Gprasp1, Tuba1a, Kifc2, Rsrp1, and Tubb2a, with Jun also increased. Neuronal PP2A inhibition can activate c-Jun, but the PP2A literature does not document this Ppp2r1a-to-microtubule/RNA-processing transcript response.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells produced a broad 1665-gene response with Kifc2, Leng8, Rsrp1, and Snap25 down and Col4a1, Amy1, and Jun up. PP2A-JNK and PPP2R1A-SREBP1 work gives partial support for immediate-early and lipid signaling, but the large Amy1/RNA-processing/synaptic program is not directly predictable.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in MB glutamatergic cells gave 648 downstream DEGs, including Amy1, Pcsk1n, Jun, and Insig1 up-regulation with Leng8, Rsrp1, and Kifc2 down-regulation. PP2A inhibition provides an indirect c-Jun expectation and PPP2R1A disruption can activate an SREBP1 lipid axis, but the dominant Amy1/RNA-processing module lacks a documented target-specific direction.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in MB/P/MY GABA cells changed 271 downstream genes with Rsrp1, Pabpn1, and Kifc2 down and Pcsk1n, Ccl25, Stmn4, and Insig1 up. The Insig1 component is indirectly compatible with PPP2R1A/SREBP1 literature, but no paper links Ppp2r1a loss to the larger Ccl25/Stmn4/RNA-processing pattern.

Ppp2r1a perturbation in P/MY/Pineal glutamatergic cells produced 105 downstream DEGs, with Kifc2, Rsrp1, and Pabpn1 decreased and Jun, Jund, and Stmn4 increased. PP2A loss can activate the JNK-c-Jun pathway, but that leaves the pineal RNA-processing and Stmn4 effects indirect and directionally underdetermined.
The only downstream DEG after Ppp2r1a perturbation in CB GABA cells was Leng8 down-regulation. The pair-level search for Ppp2r1a or PP2A Aalpha control of Leng8 did not find a specific bridge.

Psmb4 perturbation in L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic cells caused 1221 downstream DEGs, with broad synaptic/neuron-associated decreases and proteasome-stress genes such as Bax, Ddit3, Psmc6, and Psme4 increased. PSMB4 loss is documented to impair proteasome assembly/activity and induce stress programs, and neuronal PSMB4-containing proteasomes regulate the synaptic proteome, matching the stress-compensation direction while leaving individual synaptic transcript decreases less directly mapped.

Psmb4 perturbation in L2-3 IT CTX glutamatergic cells produced only 19 downstream DEGs, headed by Cacnb3 and Kcnj9 decreases with Rangap1, Mroh1, Dhx40, and Sacs increases. Searches for PSMB4 or proteasome beta-4 links to this calcium-channel/nuclear-transport set did not find a target-to-response bridge.

cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
summary: Psmb4 perturbation in L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic cells changed 338 downstream genes, with synaptic genes such as Gria2, Slc22a17, Rtn4r, and Akap5 decreased and stress/proteasome genes including Ddit3, Bax, and Psmc6 increased. PSMB4 loss reduces proteasome function and induces proteostasis stress in the literature, which predicts the compensatory stress direction; the synaptic down-regulation is consistent with neuronal proteasome disruption but less gene-specific.

cell_type: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
summary: Psmb4 perturbation in L2-3 IT PIR/AON/ENT glutamatergic cells changed 51 genes and included Psmd4 up-regulation within a mixed Pcbp1, Bex2, Eprs, and Sf3b2 response. PSMB4 loss can trigger proteasome-stress compensation, but the observed pair contains only a small proteasome component and no direct literature bridge for the main RNA-binding genes.

Psmb4 perturbation in L5 ET CTX glutamatergic cells had three downstream DEGs: Pkm and Uchl1 increased and Sort1 decreased. A pair-specific search for PSMB4 regulation of Pkm, Uchl1, or Sort1 found ubiquitin-proteasome background for UCHL1 but no specific bridge from Psmb4 loss to this transcript pattern.

Psmb4 perturbation in NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic cells caused 489 downstream DEGs with Gria2, Rims1, and Slc17a7 decreased and proteasome or stress genes including Bax, Ddit3, Psmd4, and Psme4 increased. Published PSMB4 knockdown or mutation decreases proteasome function and induces compensatory stress, agreeing with the stress arm of this response.

Psmb4 perturbation in CTX-CGE GABA cells produced a 43-gene response led by Erbb4, Ptprn2, Zcchc18, and Syt1 down-regulation plus Cpsf3, Ypel5, and Psme4 up-regulation. The pair-level search did not find a PSMB4-specific connection to the dominant Erbb4/synaptic/RNA-processing response, and the lone Psme4 increase was not enough to assign a proteasome-stress flag.

Psmb4 perturbation in Pvalb GABA cells generated 1090 downstream DEGs and included up-regulated Psme4, Psmc6, Atf3, Ddit3, and Bax alongside Kcnip2 and Tmem44 decreases. The PSMB4 literature predicts impaired proteasome function with NFE2L1/ATF3 stress compensation after Psmb4 loss, matching this pair.

Psmb4 perturbation in Sst GABA cells produced 402 downstream DEGs, decreasing Gria2 and Ahi1 while increasing Psmc6, Clu, Ddit3, Sqstm1, and Bax. Loss of PSMB4 is documented to impair the proteasome and induce stress responses, so the proteasome/autophagy and apoptotic-stress increases agree with prior direction.

Psmb4 perturbation in CNU-MGE GABA cells changed 1142 downstream genes, including Syt3, Slc22a17, and Kifc2 decreases and Naa50, Ddit3, Psme4, and Sqstm1 increases. Direct PSMB4 loss-of-function studies predict proteasome impairment and a compensatory stress response, matching the Ddit3/Psme4/Sqstm1 arm of the measured program.

The only downstream DEG after Psmb4 perturbation in CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells was Syt7 down-regulation. Searches for a PSMB4 or proteasome beta-4 relationship to Syt7 did not find a direct or partial target-to-effect bridge.

Psmb4 perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY GABA cells caused 1127 downstream DEGs, with Kifc2 and Atp1a3 reduced and Lonp1, Atf3, Ddit3, Bax, and Psme4 increased. PSMB4 disruption is known to reduce proteasome activity and induce ATF3 and proteasome-recovery programs, agreeing with the direction of the stress signature.

Psmb4 perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic cells yielded 2098 downstream DEGs, lowering Slc17a6, Zcchc18, and Adam11 while increasing Ddit3, Hsph1, Psme4, Sqstm1, and Atf3. The documented consequence of PSMB4 loss is proteasome dysfunction with integrated stress and compensatory proteasome expression, which matches the Ddit3/Atf3/Psme4/Sqstm1 direction.

Psmb4 perturbation in MH-LH/TH glutamatergic cells changed 370 downstream genes, including Pdrg1, BC005537, Atf3, Psme4, and Hsph1 increases and Stmn2 and Atp1a3 decreases. PSMB4 loss directly impairs proteasome activity and induces stress markers such as Atf3 in published knockdown systems, agreeing with the stress-compensation module here.

Psmb4 perturbation in TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells caused 1102 downstream DEGs, lowering Atp2b1, Gabrb2, and Tuba1a while increasing Psmc4, Ddit3, Bax, and Sqstm1. Direct PSMB4 loss-of-function literature predicts proteasome impairment and stress/autophagy compensation, matching those increases.

Psmb4 perturbation in MB glutamatergic cells generated 2489 downstream DEGs with Atp1b1, Dnm1, and Atp1a3 down and BC005537, Ubc, Ddit3, Psme4, and Atf3 up. The observed stress/proteasome-compensatory response is the expected direction from PSMB4 loss reducing proteasome function; the broad synaptic repression is compatible with neuronal proteasome disruption but not individually mapped.

Psmb4 perturbation in MB/P/MY GABA cells changed 1996 downstream genes, including Lonp1, Ddit3, Sqstm1, and Atf3 up-regulation with Syp, Nsg1, Gria2, and Atp1a3 down-regulation. PSMB4 loss is known to compromise the proteasome and activate stress programs, so the stress arm agrees with prior evidence while the synaptic-gene decreases remain a less direct part of the same pair.

Psmb4 perturbation in CB GABA cells produced 27 downstream DEGs, mostly increases including BC005537, Chpf2, Psme4, Psmc6, and Sqstm1. PSMB4 loss impairs proteasome activity and induces compensatory proteasome and stress genes in published knockdown systems, agreeing with the Psme4/Psmc6/Sqstm1 direction.

Tpr perturbation in L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic cells produced 478 downstream DEGs with Pigm, Zfp281, Ranbp6, Xpo1, and Tob1 up-regulated and RNA-processing genes including Srrm2, Ddx17, and Srsf5 reduced. TPR knockdown perturbs tRNA export, NXF1-dependent RNA surveillance, HSF1/HSP70 export, and CRM1-dependent trafficking, but those studies do not predict these specific Ranbp6/Pigm/splicing transcript directions.

Tpr perturbation in L2-3 IT CTX glutamatergic cells produced 8 downstream DEGs, including Usp34 and Ranbp6 up and Ttc3, Zmym3, and Smpd4 down. The presence of Ranbp6 gives a partial nuclear-transport bridge to TPR biology, but no literature links Tpr loss to this sparse Usp34/Ttc3/Ranbp6 pattern in a directional way.

cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
summary: The only downstream DEG after Tpr perturbation in L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic cells was Pigm up-regulation. A pair-level search for a TPR or nuclear-basket link to Pigm regulation found no specific direct or indirect relationship.

Tpr perturbation in L5 ET CTX glutamatergic cells had 8 downstream DEGs, led by Ice1 down, Aff4 and Klhl9 up, Pcsk5 down, and later Lig4, Myo9a, and Ranbp6 increases. Searches for TPR relationships to Ice1, Aff4, Klhl9, Pcsk5, or Ranbp6 did not find a biologically specific bridge for this pair.
Tpr perturbation in CNU-MGE GABA cells had two downstream DEGs, Camkk2 and Arhgap5, both increased. Searches for TPR links to Camkk2 or Arhgap5 did not identify any target-to-response literature.

Tpr perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY GABA cells changed 153 downstream genes, with Ranbp6, Pigm, and Yod1 increased and Amy1, Rnpc3, Ddx17, Snhg11, and Ogt decreased. TPR is directly implicated in RNA export and nuclear-pore trafficking, giving a partial bridge to the RNA-processing and transport signature but not a gene-specific prediction.

Tpr perturbation in CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic cells produced 38 downstream DEGs, mainly Pigm, Nap1l5, Kmt2e, Jrkl, Mob1a, Slmap, and Arhgap5 up-regulation with Amy1 down-regulation. Exact searches for TPR connections to Pigm, Amy1, Arhgap5, and the chromatin-associated genes did not find a specific bridge.

Tpr perturbation in MH-LH/TH glutamatergic cells produced 320 downstream DEGs with Ranbp6, Xpo1, and Chd9 increased and Snhg11, Leng8, and Srrm2 decreased. TPR knockdown perturbs CRM1/XPO1-related trafficking and NXF1-pathway RNA quality control, but the path to these transcript-level changes is incomplete.

Tpr perturbation in TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells generated 2262 downstream DEGs, increasing Xpo1, Flrt2, and Tob1 and decreasing Leng8, Ogt, Ddx17, Rnpc3, and Srsf5. TPR is part of NXF1-associated RNA surveillance, neuronal intron-retention control, and nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, which is specific to the RNA/export module but insufficient to predict the observed signs.

Tpr perturbation in MB glutamatergic cells caused the largest Tpr response, with 3109 downstream DEGs including Tob1, Chd9, Ranbp6, and Pigm up and Snhg11, Leng8, Rnpc3, and Srsf5 down. The nuclear-basket literature directly places TPR in tRNA export, mRNA surveillance, and neuronal intron-retention control, but it does not resolve why this acute response should induce Pigm/Ranbp6 while repressing these RNA-processing genes.

Tpr perturbation in MB/P/MY GABA cells changed 401 downstream genes, with Ranbp6 and Med13 increased and Wsb1, Ptprs, Kifc2, Amy1, and Rnpc3 decreased. TPR loss is known to affect RNA export and nuclear transport, partially matching the Ranbp6/Rnpc3 response, but no cited work establishes this mixed direction.

Tpr perturbation in CB GABA cells produced 72 downstream DEGs including Pigm, Atf1, and Atxn7l3b increases with Ogt, Snhg11, and Dnajb5 decreases. Searches for TPR links to the Pigm/Ogt/Snhg11/Atf1 pattern did not find a specific pair-level bridge.
